title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.6.1, 19.5.8, 19.4.10
description:
Update: On November 25, 2026, we backported the fix for CVE-2026-132825 and the other vulnerabilities disclosed in the Ruby security advisory to versions 19.3.10, 19.2.11, 19.1.11, 19.0.12, and 18.11.15 of GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE). Self-managed GitLab administrators running older versions of GitLab CE and EE can now upgrade to these versions to apply these security fixes.

On November 20, 2026, we released versions 19.6.1, 19.5.8, 19.4.10 for GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition.

These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already running a patched version. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action. GitLab Dedicated was previously protected through internal-only releases 19.5.7 and 19.4.9, which contained interim mitigations for these vulnerabilities; all fixes from those releases are also included in 19.5.8 and 19.4.10.

GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases: scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays. For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ. You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here.
